title: Reset & Roll
intro: Fifteen minutes with a foam roller, after training or on the evening of a hard day.
Slow is the whole thing. Stop on the sore spots and breathe there rather than sawing back and forth.

before.label: Never roll
before.text: Your lower back, so stay above the bottom of your ribcage. Also the front or side of your neck, the back of your knee, the inside of your elbow, your armpit or right into the groin crease. Nothing that's swollen, hot, bruised or freshly hurt.

before.label: Leave that spot alone
before.text: If something grabbed during play and it's still sore now, leave it alone and get it looked at. If it's sharp, or you get pins and needles, back off.

before.label: Swollen calf
before.text: If one calf is swollen, warm or tender and you didn't strain it playing, don't roll it and see a doctor the same day.

good: Slow from the ankle up, cross the other leg on top for more pressure
Stop on the sore spots and breathe
Face down, slow from knee to hip
Bend and straighten the knee while you pause on a spot

exercises.name: Glute Roll

good: Sit on the roller, cross one ankle over the opposite knee and lean into it
Small movements — you are hunting one spot
bad: Sitting on it without actually loading one side

exercises.note: This is the one most players skip and most need.

good: Roller across the upper back, hands behind the head, ribs down
Pause and breathe at each level
On your side, arm overhead, roller under the armpit
Small movements, pause where it bites
Knees wide, hips back to the heels, arms long
Breathe into your back and let it widen
bad: Rushing to get to the breathing

exercises.name: Box Breathing

good: In for four, hold four, out for four, hold four
Lie down, one hand on the belly, only that hand moves
bad: Straining to hold the counts — shorten to three

exercises.note: This is the part that actually switches you off, so do not cut it short.
